title: Limitation period - the silent killer of strong civil cases
p1:
A case can be legally strong, backed by facts and evidence… and still fail before it even reaches the courtroom.

The reason? A deadline most people never notice.
p2:
Many believe that having a valid claim is enough to seek justice anytime. The surprising truth is that the law often gives you a limited window to act.

This time limit is called the limitation period. Once it expires, even a genuine claim may become difficult or impossible to enforce.
p3:
Think of it like a legal expiry date. The clock may start from the moment an incident happens, when a right is violated, or when a person becomes aware of the issue, depending on the type of case.

The biggest mistake is waiting until the dispute becomes serious before taking action. Preserving documents, seeking advice early, and knowing the deadline can protect an otherwise strong case.

A winning argument is useless if it arrives too late.
conclusion: Have you ever seen a good case fail because someone missed a legal deadline? What was the lesson learned?
